description.narrative:
In March 2020, Guidelines for the Assessment of the Implementation of ECOWAS Protocols on Free Movement of Persons were presented to ECOWAS Member States at a regional workshop held in Accra, Ghana. The implementation of the Protocols is essential for promoting and protecting the human rights and fundamental rights of migrants including migrant workers. The Guidelines had been developed by the ECOWAS Commission Directorate on Free Movement and Tourism and the Social Affairs Department. The regional workshop was also an opportunity to discuss the effective operationalization of the Guidelines and raise awareness and knowledge of ECOWAS Focal Points in Member States on relevant ECOWAS Protocols and their implementation. Since the presentation of the Guidelines, a total of eleven country work plans have been developed by ECOWAS Member States outlining concrete steps on how to advance the Guidelines at the national level.
Following an assessment of the status of child labour in the ECOWAS region, ECOWAS developed and finalized the second phase of the Regional Action Plan (RAP) on Child Labour for validation of the Child Labour Experts of the ECOWAS Region in 2021 and endorsement by the ECOWAS Ministers of Labour and Employment. National focal points have started implementing the elements of the action plan.
The structure of the SDG itself had been revised including through linking it with the Labour Ministers' Meeting to ensure that decisions taken by the SDF General Assembly would be transferred to and endorsed by the Labour Ministers' meeting. A monitoring framework for the implementation of the ECOWAS Free Movement Protocols was developed and validated. With support from the European Union, the ILO provided technical and financial support to the ECOWAS Commission Directorate of Free Movement and Tourism and the Social Affairs Department in assessing and developing an evaluation and monitoring mechanism for the implementation of the ECOWAS Protocols on Free Movement of Persons by ECOWAS Member States. The assessment was conducted in 2016 and the resulting report was reviewed and validated in 2017. Monitoring tools were developed in 2019 and early 2020 and presented to ECOWAS Member States at a regional training of national focal points in early March 2020 in Accra, Ghana.
With the support of the European Union as well as the Netherlands, the ILO also supported the engagement of a consultant who conducted the evaluation of the implementation of the ECOWAS Regional Action Plan on Child Labour and the development of the 2nd phase of the Regional Action Plan.
